title: Cross-month reader rule: _latest_sfs orders by (lastseen DESC, load_dt DESC)
objective: In etl4/vault/marts.py, add a dedicated _latest_sfs(sfs) helper that picks the latest sat_flight_summary row per hk_flight by sorting on (lastseen DESC, load_dt DESC) with a stable sort, instead of load_dt-only. Route build_fact_flight_for_ym's sat_flight_summary reduction through the new helper. Reader-side implementation of ADR 2026-11-13 Risk 1 (cross-month flights produce two rows with identical hk_flight but different lastseen / load_dt; the earlier-month row can carry a newer load_dt if its ingest was rerun).
unblocks: T-16 (data-engineer review of T-14/T-15 mart schema contract)
Follow-up ADR entry in etl4/docs/decisions.md documenting the reader-side rule (arch 9.3)

files_changed.note: Added _latest_sfs(sfs) dedicated reducer with (hk_flight ASC, lastseen DESC, load_dt DESC) stable sort + drop_duplicates(subset=['hk_flight'], keep='first'). _latest_per left untouched (still used by sat_aircraft_identity, link_flight_aircraft, link_flight_route -- none of which carry lastseen). build_fact_flight_for_ym now calls _latest_sfs(sfs) in place of _latest_per(sfs, ['hk_flight']). Removed the stale 'T-15 refines the sat_flight_summary variant ...' sentence from _latest_per's docstring (CLAUDE.md section 3.7 bans task refs in comments) and replaced it with a precise WHY in the new _latest_sfs docstring.

Unit-level smoke directly on marts._latest_sfs. Five cases: (a) Feb row has later lastseen and later load_dt -> Feb wins; (b) Jan row has later load_dt (ingest rerun), Feb has later lastseen -> Feb still wins (the pre-T-15 miscall); (c) identical lastseen -> later load_dt wins; (d) a second hk_flight passes through untouched; (e) NA lastseen loses to a real one. Also an empty-frame smoke. Uses dtypes matching raw_vault.build_sat_flight_summary (lastseen/firstseen UTC-aware). Prints 'LATEST_SFS SMOKE OK'. No Postgres, no filesystem fixtures.

integration_points.reads: No new reads. marts._latest_sfs consumes the same per-ym sat_flight_summary partition (data/silver/vault/sat_flight_summary/ym=<YM>/part.parquet) that _latest_per consumed pre-T-15.
integration_points.writes: No new writes. Downstream surface (fact_flight/ym=<YM>/part.parquet) is byte-equivalent on the T-14 small-fixture case (confirmed by T-14 smoke pass) and semantically-equivalent on single-ym inputs (one sfs row per hk_flight within one ym -> both _latest_per and _latest_sfs pick that row).
consumers: etl4/vault/postgres_sink.py (T-17 DONE, reads fact_flight/ym=<ym>/part.parquet) -- unaffected on single-ym inputs; benefits when postgres-side ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET lastseen=EXCLUDED.lastseen replays a cross-month pair.

contract_deviations: Objective text 'change _latest_sfs()' presupposes a function with that name. Pre-T-15 the file had only a shared _latest_per (used by sat_aircraft_identity, link_flight_aircraft, link_flight_route, sat_flight_summary). Chosen path: introduce the specifically-named _latest_sfs(sfs) helper (matches arch section 9.1 R1 and 0 row 8) and route the sat_flight_summary call site through it. _latest_per is left alone -- changing its sort would break the other three call sites which have no lastseen column, and sniffing for lastseen inside _latest_per would be hidden behavior.

Objective lists 'etl4/vault/marts.py (surgical -- ONLY the _latest_sfs sort/dedup; do NOT edit the build functions)'. The single-token routing change on line 135 (from _latest_per(sfs, ['hk_flight']) to _latest_sfs(sfs)) technically edits build_fact_flight_for_ym. This is unavoidable: adding a new helper has no reader if the call site is not switched. No other build-function logic changed.
spec_gaps_resolved: Per-ym scoping gap (acknowledged for T-16). sfs is read with ym_filter=ym, so the Jan and Feb rows for a cross-month flight never land in the same _latest_sfs call. The reducer change therefore does NOT dedupe cross-month pairs inside a single build_fact_flight_for_ym invocation; both rows reach fact_flight/ym=M and fact_flight/ym=M+1. Dedup happens at the postgres_sink UPSERT layer (arch section 4 line 862: ON CONFLICT (hk_flight) DO UPDATE SET lastseen=EXCLUDED.lastseen). Forward-chronological runs are correct (Feb overwrites Jan); a rewind-and-rebuild of month M alone would rewrite the Jan row and clobber the Feb lastseen. The _latest_sfs change IS necessary and sufficient when both rows do happen to share a frame (e.g., migration re-reads spanning multiple ym, or a future globally-scoped reducer). See architecture section 9.3 'follow-up ADRs for the orchestrator' -- a new ADR entry documenting this reader-side rule is listed as post-T-15 work.
risks_for_t16: Rewind-month-M-only scenario can revert the cross-month lastseen in fact_flight (Postgres). Architecture section 9.1 R1 claims _latest_sfs mitigates this; in the current per-ym-scoped reader shape, the mitigation only holds for cases where both rows land in one DataFrame. A separate rewind-contract check (or a globally-scoped post-build reducer) is needed to close R1 fully. Flag for T-16 discussion.
